deleteConfirmDescription: Are you sure you want to delete this row?
Name: Name
dtPagePropsIntro: Start here for DataTable usage. Install the package, then use the props reference below to configure behavior and styling.
dtPagePropsSetup: Minimal setup: tableId, rowKey, columnsInfo, dataSource, pagination. Use serverMode for server-driven paging/search/filter/sort; add paginationState, sortState, onPageChange, and onSortChange when you control state from outside.
dtPageBasicDesc: Search, client pagination, column resize, column visibility, and row actions with delete confirmation.
dtPageBasicSetup: Uses paginationState + onPageChange, searchValue + onSearch, columnResize, and actions with deleteModalConfig.
dtPageGroupsDesc: Use Group by to switch between department and role; groupConfig updates getGroupLabel and order. Group order follows groupConfig.order when provided.
dtPageUsersDemoDesc: Flat table (no grouping) showcasing column render: avatars via Dicebear, Ant Design Tags and Tooltip, icons, localized dates with dayjs, and Typography. Use the Row groups demo to experiment with groupConfig.
dtPageUsersDemoSetup: columnsInfo uses render for most columns: Avatar + stacked name/email, colored Tags for role and status, map icon + location, dayjs absolute + relative joined date. See Row groups for getGroupLabel and Group by.
dtPageFiltersDesc: Multi-select and date presets in the toolbar. Wire filterValues and onFilterChange for controlled filters.
dtPageFiltersSetup: filters: multi options for status and category; date filter on Updated. This demo filters the dataset in memory based on filter state.
dtPageSelectionDesc: Selection column, per-row and bulk bookmark, and refresh. Use onSelectionChange and onBookmarkChange to sync state.
dtPageSelectionSetup: onRefresh is passed to show the refresh control. Selection and bookmark keys are echoed above the table.
dtPageServerDesc: DummyJSON (dummyjson.com) exposes products with server-side limit, skip, sortBy, order, search (/products/search?q=…), and category (/products/category/:slug or search + category). Categories for the filter come from GET /products/categories. The table only maps the JSON response to rows—no client-side filtering or sorting.
dtPageServerSetup: Build the request URL from paginationState, debounced search, sortState (mapped to sortBy/order), and the first selected category slug when using the multi filter. Pass total from the API response to pagination.totalItems. If several categories are selected, only the first is sent (DummyJSON accepts one category per request).
dtPageServerLoadError: Could not load products from the API.
dtPageSortDesc: Click sortable headers to change order. In client mode, sorting is handled internally. In server mode, use onSortChange and pass sortState.
dtPageSortSetup: Set sortable: true on columns. For server sorting, pass serverMode + sortState + onSortChange and return sorted rows from your API.
dtPageColorsDesc: Use customColors to override light mode, dark mode, and primary accent colors.
dtPageColorsSetup: customColors={{ primaryColor, lightMode, darkMode }}. Use top theme toggle to switch light and dark previews.
dtPageLoadingDesc: Pass loading to show Ant Design’s table loading overlay. Toggle below to preview.
dtPageLoadingSetup: loading={boolean}. Typically tied to an async fetch lifecycle.
dtPageLayoutDesc: maxTableHeight keeps the header and footer fixed while the table body scrolls. Also demonstrates onRowClick, renderToolbarLeft, renderToolbarRight, className, disableSelectionAndBookmark, and hideColumnOptions.
dtPageLayoutSetup: maxTableHeight="min(320px, 45vh)" with page size 50 so many rows stay on one page and scroll inside the body. Toggle hide columns to try hideColumnOptions.
dtLayoutClickHint: Click a data row to trigger onRowClick.
dtPagePlaygroundDesc: Paste a JSON array of row objects, optionally define columns, then toggle props and watch the table update. JSON is validated as you work; use the toolbar buttons to format or load samples. The live preview stays pinned beside the controls while you scroll, so you can edit at the bottom and still see the table.
dtPagePlaygroundSetup: Rows must be a JSON array of objects with the same keys. Set row key to a field that is unique per row (e.g. id). Leave columns empty to infer headers from the first row, or paste columns with id, label, and dataIndex.
dtPlaygroundRowsHelp: Paste an array like [{ "id": 1, "name": "…" }, …]. Invalid JSON shows an error below.
dtPlaygroundErr_notArray: Rows must be a JSON array.
dtPlaygroundErr_rowNotObject: Each row must be a non-null object.
dtPlaygroundErr_json: Invalid JSON. Check brackets, quotes, and commas.
dtPlaygroundColumnsHelp: Optional: array of { id, label, dataIndex, … }. Leave empty to infer columns from the first data row.
dtPlaygroundColumnsPlaceholder: Leave empty to infer from row data…
dtPlaygroundColErr_notArray: Columns must be a JSON array.
dtPlaygroundColErr_columnShape: Each column needs id, label, and dataIndex.
dtPlaygroundWarnRowKey: Some rows are missing the row key field — keys may be unstable.
dtPlaygroundFixJsonHint: Fix row or column JSON to see the live table.
dtPlaygroundLastClickEmpty: Click a data row in the table — the row key field value from the left panel is echoed here.
dtPlaygroundColumnsEmpty: Columns field is empty — inferring from data.
docsDataTablePropsIntro: Main props to configure DataTable behavior, data handling, and UI customization.
docsChooseAdapterTitle: Choose an adapter (RTK Query vs React Query)
isWhatUiDoesPoint1: Renders a vertical scroll container with your cards.
isWhatUiDoesPoint2: Shows an initial loader while the first page is loading.
isWhatUiDoesPoint3: Shows an empty state when there are no items.
isWhatUiDoesPoint4: Calls onLoadMore when users reach the bottom and shows a fetch-more loader.
isHowItFitsTitle: How it fits with RTK Query and React Query
isHowItFitsIntro: You stay in charge of the data layer. InfiniteScrollUI only handles list rendering and loading states; wrappers connect it to your query library.
isHowItFitsPoint1: InfiniteScrollRTK connects page-based RTK Query endpoints and passes normalized items/loading flags to the UI.
isHowItFitsPoint2: InfiniteScrollRQ uses useInfiniteQuery and flattens pages into one list with hasNextPage.
isPropsIntro: Main props for the infinite scroll list and wrappers.
isPropHeightClassDesc: CSS class applied to the outer container to control height (for example, a fixed panel height).
isPropUseQueryDesc: Injected hook that fetches one page. Receives { query: { page, ... }, tag } and returns data/loading state.
isPropBuildQueryArgsDesc: Builds the { query, tag } payload for each page request.
isPropSelectItemsDesc: Maps raw response to an items array for rendering.
isPropSelectHasNextDesc: Returns true while there are more pages to fetch based on API response metadata.
isPropGetKeyDesc: Returns a stable key for each item to avoid duplicates when appending pages.
isPropRenderItemDesc: Render function for each item card/row.
isPropEnabledDesc: When false, the list resets internal state and skips querying.
isPropEmptyStateDesc: Node rendered when no items exist after initial load.
isPropClassNameDesc: Extra classes for the outer container.
isPropThresholdPxDesc: Pixel distance from the bottom that triggers next-page loading.
isPropResetKeyDesc: When changed, resets pages and items (useful for search/filter changes).
isPropRenderInitialLoaderDesc: Custom node for first-page loading state.
isPropRenderFetchingLoaderDesc: Custom node shown while loading additional pages.
isReactPageDescription: How to build an infinite products feed using React Query's useInfiniteQuery hook.
isReactPageSetup: Scroll inside the panel to load next pages. InfiniteScrollList handles scroll and append behavior.
isReactHowToTitle: How to create the React Query hook
isReactHowToDesc: The core is useInfiniteQuery with getNextPageParam reading skip/limit from API response.
isRtkPageDescription: Real-world infinite scroll with RTK Query and InfiniteScrollList.
isRtkPageSetup: Scroll inside the panel to trigger loading the next page.
isRtkHowToTitle: How to create the RTK Query API
isRtkHowToDesc: Use createApi with serializeQueryArgs, merge, and forceRefetch to append pages under one cache key.
qtRtkDescription: QueryTable stays framework-agnostic. You inject a { tag, query } => useQuery adapter. URL state is handled by parseTableState + serializeTableState.
qtRtkSetup: This page hides RTK Query store/API setup and focuses on adapter shape + URL persistence.
qtReactDescription: Same QueryTable API, only the injected useQuery adapter changes. URL persistence stays in the page.
qtReactSetup: React Query provider is set at app level. This snippet focuses on adapter + URL persistence.
cmDrawerDescription: Query-driven CRUD workflow with add/edit forms rendered in drawer by default.
cmDrawerSetup: This demo uses RTK Query for list + add/update/delete mutations.
cmModalDescription: Same API as drawer mode, but form surface is modal for focused editing.
cmModalSetup: Same API, with RTK Query mutations and modal form surface.
dfDefaultViewDescription: Use the default variant when the form should live directly inside the page layout.
dfDefaultViewSetup: Create-style inline form using field-level validation and typed field config.
dfInlineFormDesc: Inline form with avatar, tags, and status switch.
dfModalViewDescription: Use the modal variant for focused create/edit flows above current page content.
dfModalViewSetup: Best for compact forms that require full attention.
dfModalFormDesc: Modal form with inline validation and typed field config.
dfDrawerViewDescription: Use the drawer variant for side-panel workflows that keep page context.
dfDrawerViewSetup: Great for multi-field tasks while keeping actions visible.
dfDrawerFormDesc: Side-panel form with textarea and color selection.
dfColorsDescription: Customize DynamicForm color tokens for light and dark mode.
dfColorsSetup: Adjust token values and preview the same palette across inline, modal, and drawer variants.
dfInlineColorOverrideDesc: Inline variant with live color token overrides.
dfModalColorOverrideDesc: Modal variant using the same custom color tokens.
dfDrawerColorOverrideDesc: Drawer variant using the same custom color tokens.
homeHeroSubtitle: React data kit gives you practical, production-ready building blocks for data tables, query-driven views, dynamic forms, and infinite lists in one playground.
homeStackNote: Works with RTK Query and React Query.
homeFeatureDataTableDesc: Client and server patterns, grouped rows, filtering, selection, and color customization with practical examples.
homeFeatureQueryTableDesc: Try query-driven table patterns with simple examples and adapter swaps between RTK Query and React Query.
homeFeatureDynamicFormDesc: Build inline, modal, and drawer forms from typed config with shared validation and theming patterns.
homeFeatureInfiniteScrollDesc: Ship endless product feeds with reusable list UI and clean integration points for your query library.
homeContribPrompt: Want to contribute as a developer?
contribSubtitle: Contribute like you would on GitHub: fork, branch, implement, validate, and open a pull request.
contribWorkflowClone: Clone your fork to your machine.
contribWorkflowBranch: Create a focused feature/fix branch from main.
contribRunIntro: Use npm for this project workspace. Run the playground to validate UI behavior while coding.
contribChecksIntro: Before pushing, run type checks and production builds for both package and playground.
contribPrCommit: Commit with a clear message describing the change intent.
contribPrPush: Push your branch to your fork on GitHub.
contribPrOpen: Open a pull request against the main branch and include test notes/screenshots when useful.
contribFinalNote: Keep pull requests focused and small when possible. If your change affects behavior, document the before/after clearly in the PR description and update the relevant playground page so contributors and users can see the new behavior.
